data.name: Garv
data.gender_notes: Garv is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Garv is a Sanskrit word derived from the root 'grh' which means 'to dwell'. This name symbolizes the feeling of self-respect, pride, and ego. It is believed that the person named Garv is self-confident, courageous, and has a strong sense of self-worth. The name Garv carries the meaning “Pride, Self-respect, Ego” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Garv usually hope their child will grow to embody pride, self-respect, ego and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A sense of self-worth, self-respect, and inner pride.
data.etymology: Garv belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pride, Self-respect, Ego.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Garv total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Garv encompasses both positive and negative connotations in the Hindu culture, depending on the context. On a positive note, it signifies a sense of pride and self-respect, instilling a deep sense of satisfaction and self-confidence. On the other hand, when taken to an extreme, Garv may lead to arrogance, narcissism, and an inflated ego.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Garv represents the innate dignity and sacredness of an individual's being. It is the understanding that every living being is a unique expression of the Divine and is thus worthy of respect and love. The spiritual significance of the name Garv lies in reminding us to cherish our own worth and worthiness while embodying humility and compassion for others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Garv symbolizes self-pride and self-esteem. It represents an individual's recognition and appreciation of their inherent worth and abilities. This name encourages one to cultivate a healthy sense of self-confidence and self-respect.

vedic_reference.note: Garv is a common Hindi word, but it does not have a direct Sanskrit origin. The Sanskrit term Garvam comes closest in meaning and is derived from the Sanskrit words rajas (king) and rupam (wealth).
